issues.body: I have been investigating this repository and ROASMI paper and found several issues. All compounds present in the 219 are also present in 429. Also all their retention times match exactly. It seems to me that confusion stems from the fact that this is basically the same dataset pulled from different sources. The 429 cites the paper both probably used. It seems that in that paper they split data into training and validation sets. The 219 contains only the training dataset. While the 429 contains both training and validation. Also the metadata provided in the 429 seems to be incorrect. The solvent system used is different.

issues.title: Fix check_metadata() to generate heptafluorobutyric columns
issues.body:
The canonical schema (example/0259_metadata.tsv + all processed_data/*) was upgraded to 185 columns including eluent.{A,B,C,D}.heptafluorobutyric(.unit) in commits 56f6cefcb and 0b80b88, but check_metadata() in helper_functions.R was never updated to emit them. As a result, re-running metadata_standardize.R on any dataset whose raw data lacks HFBA (e.g. 0002) produces only 177 columns, and order_metadata_tsv.py then fails its column-set assertion against the 185-column 0259 template.

This PR adds the 8 missing columns following the existing medronic block pattern (value defaults to 0, .unit defaults to NA_character_), placed immediately after each eluent.X.pH to match the canonical order. Datasets that already carry HFBA columns are unaffected.

issues.title: character encoding, typo fixes, populate 'mode' for column_database.tsv
issues.body:
Hi Michael,

Please consider merging the following fixes and corrections to the column_database.tsv:

1 - latin-1 encoded special characters were converted to match the utf-8 encoding used in the rest of the file.
2 - 6 column model names with missing/corrupted special characters or typos were corrected.
3 - usp codes for 8 column models were fixed where drag-down, incosistent or incorrect codes were identified.

This will help with the downstream conversion to ontology terms. The python code used for the conversion is copied below.

Best, Jon

P.S. Huge congratulations on your award!

```python
"""One-time retro fix of the RepoRT catalog: column_database.tsv -> *_fixed.tsv.

Applies three curated corrections and preserves everything else byte-for-byte:
encoding, corrupted product names (NAME_FIXES), and wrong usp codes (USP_FIXES).
Code written with assistance from Claude, reviewed by JEH.
"""

INPUT = "column_database.tsv"
OUTPUT = "column_database_fixed.tsv"

USP_COL = 6  # 0-based field index of the "usp" column
NAME_COL = 8  # 0-based field index of the "Column name" column

# Source corruptions in product names: a character became a literal "?", a mangled
# look-alike, or a letter was dropped — none recoverable by the encoding pass. Each
# maps the corrupted fragment to its verified spelling and is substituted wherever
# the name appears (the short "column" field, "Column name", and "full description").
# Fixing the fragment also merges any duplicate rows the corruption created.
NAME_FIXES = {
    "NUCLEODUR ?²": "NUCLEODUR π²",
    "COSMOSIL ?NAP": "COSMOSIL πNAP",
    "Cogent Diamond Hydride 2.?": "Cogent Diamond Hydride 2.0",
    "Cogent Diamond Hydride 2.ō": "Cogent Diamond Hydride 2.0",
    "UltraSep ES C10 ?-COOH": "UltraSep ES C10 ω-COOH",
    "ZORBAX RRHT Eclipse XDB-8": "ZORBAX RRHT Eclipse XDB-C8",  # dropped "C"
}

# Correct USP <621> code, keyed by Column name, for products whose usp column is
# wrong. Manually verified.
USP_FIXES = {
    # Excel drag-down series (usp auto-filled L1, L2, L3, ... one code per row)
    "Agilent Pursuit PAH": "L118",  # PAH phase, C18-based
    "Agilent ZORBAX RRHT Eclipse XDB-C8": "L7",  # XDB-C8 -> C8 (name fixed above)
    "Agilent ZORBAX RRHT Extend-C18": "L1",  # C18
    # stray copy errors (dominant code correct; a minority cell is a typo)
    "Agilent InfinityLab Poroshell 120 SB-C18": "L1",  # C18 (was mixed L1 / L7)
    "Nouryon-Kromasil Kromasil Classic C8": "L7",  # C8  (was mixed L7 / L1)
    "Thermo Scientific Accucore 150-C4": "L26",  # C4  (was mixed L26 / L1)
    # codes that contradict the column chemistry
    "Shimadzu Shim-pack Scepter C4-300": "L26",  # C4  (was L23 anion-exchange)
    "Thermo Scientific Accucore 150-Amide-HILIC": "L68",  # amide HILIC (was L1 C18)
}

# The stray Latin-1 byte values the catalog contains -> their intended character.
LATIN1_FIXES = {0xB5: "µ", 0xC5: "Å", 0xB2: "²"}

# fix 1: encoding — decode as UTF-8 (surrogateescape carries each stray Latin-1 byte
# through as chr(0xDC00 + byte)), then map the few that occur to their character.
text = open(INPUT, "rb").read().decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")
for byte, char in LATIN1_FIXES.items():
    text = text.replace(chr(0xDC00 + byte), char)

# fix 2: missing characters — substitute each corrupted name fragment wherever it occurs
for bad, good in NAME_FIXES.items():
    text = text.replace(bad, good)

# fix 3: usp errors — rewrite only the usp field of the named products, leaving the
# rest of every line (quoting, spacing, other columns) byte-for-byte intact
lines = text.split("\n")
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    fields = line.split("\t")
    if len(fields) > NAME_COL and fields[NAME_COL].strip() in USP_FIXES:
        fields[USP_COL] = USP_FIXES[fields[NAME_COL].strip()]
        lines[i] = "\t".join(fields)
text = "\n".join(lines)

open(OUTPUT, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(text)
print(f"wrote {OUTPUT}")
```

The file appears to contain duplicate entries, missing structure annotations, and a likely misalignment between compound names/RTs and PubChem fields.

## Observed Issues

### 1. Possible annotation shift in later rows

Rows `0052_00105`-`0052_00137` appear suspicious.  
The compound `name` and `rt` fields seem to repeat earlier compounds, but the structure annotations appear to be shifted/misaligned.

Example:

  - rt: `1.1`
  - formula: `C22H18O11`
  - PubChem CID: `65064`

These structure fields appear to correspond to `(-)-Epigallocatechin gallate`, not `Myo-inositol`.

The `comment` column contains many duplicate-related notes:
